label: alg:gb-filtration
title: Gröbner–Shirshov filtration / $E_2$ collapse
html:
Algorithm (Gröbner–Shirshov filtration with E_2 collapse). Compute the length-graded filtration on H_n(q) and assert E_2-collapse of the associated spectral sequence — every higher differential d_r (r \geq 2) vanishes.

Input

  • Braid index n, substrate parameter q.

Output

  • Length-graded decomposition H_n(q) = \bigoplus_{\ell \geq 0} F_\ell / F_{\ell - 1} where F_\ell is the span of basis elements T_w with \ell(w) \leq \ell.
  • Boolean assertion that d_r = 0 for all r \geq 2 (i.e. the spectral sequence collapses at the E_2 page).

Algorithm

1. For each ℓ from 0 to ℓ_max:
     enumerate basis elements T_w with ℓ(w) = ℓ.
2. Build the associated graded ⊕_ℓ gr_ℓ H_n(q).
3. Verify d_2 = 0 by checking that the Markov trace pairs
   gr_ℓ with gr_{ℓ + r} trivially for r > 0.
4. Return the filtration and the collapse certificate.

Correctness conditions

prop:gb-spectral-sequence asserts E_2-collapse for the GS filtration on H_n(q) in the QOU rigid-monoidal setting. The proof uses the diamond-lemma / Gröbner basis structure of the Hecke relations and is standard modulo the QOU-specific Markov coefficient z.

Complexity

O(\dim H_n(q)) basis enumeration. The collapse check is quadratic in the number of basis elements but the result is cached per (n, q) pair.

Python API entry point

Canonical compute is the script computations/gb_filtration_jet_tracker.py; run it directly to emit the witness. The Rust implementation lives in tools/hecke-engine/, called via pyhecke_native when the per-particle builders need the filtered NF.

Witness contract

Canonical witness: gb-filtration-jet-order.witness.json records the per-level filtration dimensions and the d_2 = 0 certificate.

Notes

E_2-collapse justifies treating the GS filtration as exact. Any higher differential would re-mix length levels and break the jet-order matching of Step 8.
